Supply, demand and management of fresh water.
Soil as a resource; sustainable farming.
Finite materials extracted from the Earth.

walkthroughs.body_html: Renewables need critical minerals: copper for wiring, lithium and cobalt for batteries, rare earths for turbine magnets, silicon and silver for PV. Mining can cause local pollution and rely on countries with weak labour rights, e.g. cobalt from DR Congo. Building a circular economy with reuse, recycling and substitution is essential.

Wind turbines can kill birds and bats, mitigated by siting and shut-down algorithms. Solar farms can shade ground but also boost biodiversity if planted with wildflowers and grazed sensitively. Hydro dams fragment rivers, blocking fish migration. Tidal barrages can alter estuaries. Careful environmental impact assessment is critical.

Community ownership, profit sharing and clear consultation reduce NIMBY opposition. Energy security has driven Europe to accelerate renewables since 2022. Just transition policies retrain fossil fuel workers and protect vulnerable households from energy poverty. Choosing energy futures is as much social and political as technical.
